title: Region Sentry — model availability & degradation insight run
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Objective:
Run a focused intelligence sprint across three target regions (US-East, eu-west, ap-southeast) to (1) quantify short-term probability that popular open model endpoints will experience availability or pricing disruptions over the next 90 days, and (2) detect early degradation signals (latency, fail rate, price spike) that should trigger our automated fallback rules.

Why now:
- Customers are asking for regional fallback guarantees and SLO-preserving fallbacks.
- Recent vendor rate-limiting incidents and a near-miss from March show we need deterministic triggers and visibility.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Weekly scraped availability & price matrix for a prioritized list of 18 public model endpoints (open and hosted) per region.
- Short-lived telemetry probes (synthetic workloads) that measure P95 latency, error rate, and token price per region for three workload archetypes (chat-short, chat-long, embedding-batch).
- Signal definition catalog: a small set of actionable indicators (e.g., 30% sustained P95 increase, 5x error-rate spike, or >25% price delta) that map to concrete actions in routing policies.
- A lightweight dashboard (Grafana) and dataset uploaded to GCS for analysis.
- Recommendation memo (2 pages) with immediate routing config tweaks and a proposed monitoring alert to add to Console rollouts.

Methodology / Data sources:
- Scraping vendor status pages + published pricing pages nightly (script in github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/market-sentry).
- Synthetic probes run from three regions via our dedicated test fleet (k8s job refs in repo).
- Customer telemetry correlation: sample logs from 3 highest-traffic customers (anonymized) to correlate perceived latency spike windows.
- External signals: Twitter/Discord rate-limiting reports, uptime robot pings, and partner Slack channel transcripts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard shows at least 4 weeks of consistent probe data and nightly scrapes for the 18 endpoints.
- We produce a table of prioritized fallback changes (severity -> routing action) tested in canary for the next release.
- Engineering owner (runtime) signs off on feasibility of each recommended automatic fallback.

Risks & trade-offs:
- False positives: temporary network blips could trigger unnecessary failovers; mitigate with smoothing window and composite signals.
- Cost: synthetic probes add token/GPU spend; limit to representative payloads and batch probes during low-cost windows.
- Data completeness: some providers obfuscate pricing tiers; we'll mark these as partial and use triangulation.

Artifacts & links:
- Draft PRD (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bMarketSentryPRD
- Implementation repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/market-sentry
- Grafana dashboard (provisional): https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/market-sentry/region-sentry
- Confluence notes and hypothesis log: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Market+Sentry

Next steps (owner: Liam Chen):
- 2026-03-03: land scrape script and run initial night of data (done).
- 2026-03-05: run first regional probes and validate telemetry ingest (done).
- 2026-03-10: review detection thresholds with runtime team and finalize signal set (in progress).
- 2026-03-15: expose basic dashboard and draft routing recommendations for canary test.

Longer-term: feed discovered signals into the Optimize playbook so that cost-aware fallbacks are evaluated against unit economics (next quarter).
